title: anthriscus cerefolium
intro: Anthriscus cerefolium, commonly known as chervil, is an annual herb in the carrot family native to Europe and Asia. Chervil is prized for its delicate, lacy foliage and is often used as a garnish or added to soups, salads, and sauces for its mild anise flavor. The herb has been traditionally used to aid digestion, reduce inflammation, and alleviate symptoms of anxiety and insomnia, due to its therapeutic actions of calming the nervous system and promoting relaxation. The bioactive constituents of chervil include flavonoids, volatile oils, and coumarins, which are responsible for its medicinal properties and are believed to contribute to its health benefits of reducing oxidative stress and improving immune function.
